source_evidence: When considering purchasing an annuity, it is important to remember that an insurance company’s obligations under an annuity contract are subject to its financial strength and claims-paying ability.
answer: Annuity payments depend on the insurance company’s ability to meet its obligations. This is the insurer’s credit risk: if the company has financial difficulties, it may not be able to pay what the contract promises. The contract’s payment terms therefore do not remove the importance of the insurer’s financial strength. The source recommends considering the financial strength and reputation of the company offering the annuity.
